flows.description: Reject substituted candidate code and omitted/filtered native cases; exercise owned temporary checkout success, failure and cancellation.

runtime.launch: unittest owns synthetic Git and native runner fixtures in temporary directories.
runtime.health: Real runner exit and case outcomes are checked against the reviewed inventory.
runtime.cleanup: TemporaryDirectory and linux-test-run finally blocks remove only their owned paths and process groups.

flows.description: Exercise all native domain, API, database, client, workflow, resource and billing assertions with exact individual case accounting.

runtime.launch: Vitest owns workerd, synthetic D1, GPG and temporary fixture processes; maxWorkers is two to bound native process contention.
runtime.health: Repository/API readbacks, real D1 billing metadata and SQL query plans validate behavior.
runtime.cleanup: Native teardown disposes workerd and temporary files; the helper rejects lingering owned descendants.

flows.description: Reject non-synthetic repository inputs, formatting errors, lint violations and invalid types.
Validate the existing isolated synthetic development stack configuration.
Run real synthetic reader, scanner and adversarial isolation probes, including resource exhaustion and owned-container removal.

runtime.launch: The native verifier creates named serial containers on the provisioned rootless socket using prepared immutable images.
runtime.health: Inspect plus kernel handshake and synthetic reader/scanner probes establish the runtime policy.
runtime.cleanup: The native launcher removes exact owned containers; no shared daemon or image cleanup.

flows.description: Build every workspace and enforce the native 100 KiB initial JavaScript gzip budget and lazy application boundary.
Replay all migrations and verify canonical synthetic scenario invariants in owned local D1.

runtime.launch: The native seed runner creates and resets only this checkout local scenario state.
runtime.health: Scenario readback assertions check migrations, seeds and relationships.
runtime.cleanup: Wrangler exits; disposable synthetic state remains under ignored .keel-local.

flows.description: Exercise the complete desktop/mobile browser contract, including minimal review, automatic decisions, persisted saves, layout, recovery and real synthetic document capture.

runtime.launch: Native D1 reset precedes Playwright webServer pnpm dev on checkout-specific ports; existing-server reuse is disabled.
runtime.health: Playwright waits through Vite /api/alpha, then asserts browser behavior and unchanged screenshot baselines.
runtime.cleanup: Playwright stops owned browsers/server groups; reports occupy one locked slot under .tugling/local/pilot.

requirements.description: All reviewed native cases and runner variants must execute with accepted outcomes; omitted, skipped, replaced or filtered cases fail.
Keep repository inputs synthetic, D1 canonical, financial arithmetic integer and accepted decisions/forecasts append-only.
Routine observations use recorded deterministic acceptance; identity, evidence and planning exceptions retain explicit decisions and minimal valid submission.
Use the accepted shared compositions and responsive controls, keep primary actions clear, preserve invalid drafts and saved-state behavior.
Keep GETs projection-only with fixed round trips and independent D1 billing/query-plan ceilings across positive, empty, 120-item, historical and unrelated-household cases.
Preserve combined idle, outage and useful-work budgets, bounded queue admission, unchanged replay, latency, cancellation and current authorization.
Validate external inputs and authenticate fail-closed, preserving evidence before accepted state.
Preserve reader/scanner isolation, input/output/time limits, bounded document capture/cache and backup count/bytes, integrity and exact owned cleanup.
Exercise success, failure and cancellation cleanup and explicit retained-run ownership; external seven-day collector activation remains outside this pilot.
Preserve locked bootstrap, synthetic migrations, focused commands, build validity and the existing initial JavaScript budget.
Preserve accepted source pins, merge verification, secret scan, protected deployment ordering, exact release evidence and production approval.
